To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) AICAR activates AMPK in cardiac cells and induces the expression of all three isoforms of PPARs; 2) the Ppara and the Pparg regulation are dependent on AMPK activation; 3) AICAR protects cardiac cells against high palmitate/ high insulin-induced intramyocellar lipid build-up and insulin resistance by inducing the expression of PPAR target genes.

AMPK activation by 5-amino-imidazole-4-car-boxamide riboside induces PPAR-target gene expression and protects cardiac HL-1 cells from high palmitate and high insulin-induced insulin resistance and intramyocellular lipids accumulation.
AMPK activation by the pharmacological agent AICAR protects HL-1 cardiocytes against the detrimental effects of a high palmitate and insulin treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of 1) the PPAR system, 2) the AMPK system, and 3) AICAR treatment on cardiac metabolism.
the role of AMPK and the PPARs in the regulation of cardiac metabolism and their potential contribution to the prevention of cardiac insulin resistance.
the role of AMPK in cardiac metabolic adaptation and its possible contribution to cardiac metabolic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AICAR is a promising therapeutic agent for the treatment of cardiac metabolic disorders.
AICAR protects HL-1 cells against high palmitate/insulin-induced intramyocelluar lipid build-up and insulin resistance, and that the AMPK-dependent PPAR-regulation contributes to this protection.
AMPK activation with AICAR induces PPAR-regulated transcription of genes involved in cardiac metabolic adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AICAR protects HL-1 cardiac cells against HP/HI-induced lipid accumulation and insulin resistance, at least partially, by inducing PPAR-target gene expression.
AMPK activation by the AMPK agonist AICAR induces the expression of the three Ppars, but the induction of Pparg and Ppara expression is dependent on AMPK activation.
AICAR, by activating the AMPK pathway, is able to prevent HP/HI-induced lipid accumulation, and insulin resistance in HL-1 cardiac cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AICAR, a well-known AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activator, can induce the transcriptional regulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) genes.

the AMPK-activated transcriptional program is a key mechanism for the beneficial metabolic effects of AICAR in the heart, and this may be relevant for the treatment of cardiac metabolic disorders such as diabetic cardiomyopathy.

AMPK is required for PPARα- and PPARγ-dependent gene expression in HL-1 cells, and AICAR prevents the high palmitate/ high insulin-induced intramyocellar lipid accumulation by up-regulating the expression of genes involved in fatty acid and glucose metabolism.
